name_en: Tagane Mochi — a flat, sea-cucumber-shaped rice cake of mochi and non-glutinous rice
summary_ja: もち米とうるち米を蒸してついた、なまこ形の平たい餅。青のりや大豆、しその実など混ぜる具は地域ごとに違う。正月によくつくられ、焼いたり揚げたりして食べる霞ヶ浦周辺の郷土菓子。
summary_en: Glutinous and non-glutinous rice are steamed and pounded together into a flat, sea-cucumber-shaped cake, its mix-ins — green nori, soybeans, shiso seeds — varying by town around Lake Kasumigaura. Grilled or fried, it is a New Year's favorite.

name_en: Aka Mochi — reddish sorghum-flour dumplings coated in sweet bean paste
summary_ja: 赤みを帯びたもろこし粉を湯で練り、だんご状にゆでてあんこやきなこをまぶす餅。稲や小麦が育ちにくい水害の多い地域で、もろこしだけが被害を免れたことから主食代わりに食べられてきた。
summary_en: Reddish sorghum flour is kneaded with hot water, boiled into dumplings, and coated with sweet bean paste or soybean flour. In flood-prone areas where rice and wheat often failed, sorghum alone survived, making this a stand-in staple.

name_en: Mitsume no Botamochi — an oversized rice cake made to mark a firstborn's birth
summary_ja: 第一子が生まれて3日後に、出産の疲労回復と母乳の出を願ってつくる大きなぼたもち。重箱に詰めて近所や親戚に配り、赤ちゃんの誕生を知らせる役目も担う。第一子のときだけの習わし。
summary_en: Three days after a first child is born, an oversized botamochi rice cake is made to help the mother recover and encourage her milk — packed into lacquer boxes and shared with neighbors as a way of announcing the birth, done only for the firstborn.
source_title: みつめのぼたもち 茨城県
